newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar may reach 117 yen in bullish Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dollar may reach 117 yen in bullish Tokyo.

text.p: The dollar is likely to start the first business day of the year in bullish mood and may reach 117 yen, but there will also be caution after its rapid rise overseas while Tokyo operators were away on holidays.
Commercial dollar buying at the local fixing at 0100 GMT could support the dollar's downside, while Japanese exporters and profit-takers are likely to slow its gains above 117 yen, dealers said.
The focus here is on the Tokyo stock market, with any further tumble in share prices likely to spur speculative dollar purchases against the yen, they said.

The Dow Jones industrial average on Friday jumped 101.60 points or 1.6 percent to close at 6,544.09. It was one of its biggest point gains ever. This helped push the dollar up to a fresh 45-month high of around 116.70/80 yen in New York.
The dollar edged higher in early Asia on Monday due to renewed confidence in the U.S. economy and dollar assets.
"The dollar may hit 117 yen (in Tokyo), but there will be profit-taking around there," said a trust bank dealer.
He said there was caution about the dollar's rapid rise as some operators had believed that 117 yen would be a key resistance point.

A Japanese city bank dealer said some operators in Tokyo had begun expecting the dollar to rise to around 118 yen within this month. She said Japanese exporters' sales may emerge at 117.00 yen and this might prevent the dollar from rising much on Monday, but the downside would be solid since there were many operators who needed to pick up dollars.
She and the trust bank dealer said they were also focusing on any remarks by monetary authorities that might be aimed at talking down the value of the dollar.
"The market is cautious about verbal interventions (by the Japanese authorities)," the city bank dealer said.
